info.desc: Horses is the debut studio album by American musician Patti Smith, released on November 10, 1975, on Arista Records. Smith, a fixture of the then-burgeoning New York punk rock music scene, began recording Horses with her band in 1975 after being signed to Arista Records, with John Cale being enlisted to produce the album. With its fusion of simplistic rock and roll structures and Smith's freeform, Beat poetry-infused lyrics, Horses was met with widespread critical acclaim upon its initial release. podcast.body: Patti Smith's commercial breakthrough album, released in 1975, was described as "poetry that was set on fire" and an "invocation." Produced by John Cale of The Velvet Underground, the record was characterized by a chaotic yet spiritual essence, with chaos being "kind of the point." It opened with a rewritten version of Van Morrison's "Gloria," featuring the line "Jesus died for somebody's sins but not mine," setting a tone of independence and transforming punk into art. "Horses wasn't really just music, it was kind of like this invocation. It opened with her rewriting Van Morrison's Gloria and she kind of turned it into this declaration of her own independence."

podcast.body: Patti Smith's debut album, "Horses," blended the spirituality of the Beat generation with a raw, punk sensibility, even though the term "punk" was not yet widely applied to music. This album was a vehicle for Smith to recite, scream, and challenge the traditional role of women in music. "Su primer disco, Jorge, mezclaba la espiritualidad beat con una clúdeza punk, aunque aún no se le llamara así."

podcast.body: Released at the end of November 1975, this debut album was an "epiphany moment" for outsiders and those seeking alternative forms of rock and pop. Michael Stipe of REM described buying it on release day, listening all night, and being a "changed person," calling it one of the defining moments in his life. "When Patty Smith's record came out of the end of November 1975, it was another one of those epiphany moments for weirdos, outsiders, and those who were actively searching for alternative forms of rock and pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in November 1975, this was Patti Smith's first and most important record. Its release coincided with the Sex Pistols' first gig and predated the Ramones' debut album by six months, making it a powerful and influential work for many female punks and future Riot Girls. "Patty's most important record was probably her first one, Horses, November 1975."
